_comment_hypothesis: Optional. One-sentence expectation written when launching the run (e.g., 'Higher lr with warmup should reach lower val_loss faster'). Tools must not require this field. Pair with `outcome` (filled at completion) for retrospective narrative; both fields exist only to enrich /train-compare reports — absence is normal.
_comment_mode: How much of the real workload this run actually processed. `production` = full data / full schedule, metrics are canonical. `debug` = deliberately truncated for fast iteration (sample limit, epochs=1, reduced batch). `screen` = short trial in a /train-tune screen_then_refine sweep. Set by the run skill at launch, never left null on a run that produced metrics. Metrics are ONLY comparable between runs with the same `mode` AND equivalent `scope` — a debug mAP over 20 images and a production mAP over 5000 are different quantities that happen to share a name.
_comment_steps: Every key here except `ad_hoc` is a step record `{status, at}`; nested keys are sub-steps. Resume reads this block to skip completed steps, so a skill MUST write the exact key names below — a key the template doesn't have is never recognized as completed and the step re-runs forever. `monitor` is long-running stages only (/train-run): it is re-entrant, so its `status` stays null while the job runs and infer/eval leave it `skipped`.
_comment_code: Filled at create_run.code_snapshot via lifecycle/scripts/shared/code_snapshot.py — merge that script's output dict in whole; do not hand-assemble it. Reproduction contract: `git checkout <origin_commit> && git apply <run_dir>/<dirty_patch_path>`, run from the code dir. Read `reproducible` first: false means a differing file was NOT embedded (too large), so checkout+apply rebuilds a different tree than the one that ran. `dirty_files_count` counts every entry in the patch, tracked and untracked alike — untracked files are invisible to `git diff HEAD`, and counting them as clean is how a run silently reproduces different code. `repo_subdir` is non-null when the code dir sits inside a larger repo (the github/server/null source modes put it under the project repo): the patch is then scoped to that subtree, but `origin_commit` still moves whenever anything else in the repo is committed, so it is not a stable identity for this code alone.

lineage._comment_variation_summary: Auto-computed when fork_of is set. Short human-readable diff of runtime_params vs the fork_of base, e.g., 'lr: 1e-4 → 2e-4; warmup_ratio: 0 → 0.03'. Null when fork_of is null. /train-run fills this at create_run time; tools may regenerate it from snapshots if missing.
lineage._comment_session: Optional. Set by /train-tune when this run is part of an adaptive HPO session. Format: '<YYYYMMDD>_<HHMMSS>_<slug>', matches the session directory name under stages/training/tune_sessions/. Null for ad-hoc runs (manual /train-run invocations not part of any tune session).

_comment_runtime_state: Streaming-state fields (used by long-running skills like /train-run). last_heartbeat: ISO timestamp of the last monitor check at which the job was observed to be making progress — agents detect hung jobs when (now - last_heartbeat) exceeds expected interval. last_step: most recent step number observed in the jsonl stream — lets agents read ETA without re-tailing the whole log; null for stages without step concept. latest_metrics: most recent streaming snapshot (e.g., last val_epoch's key fields) — distinct from `metrics` which holds the final/terminal numbers populated on completion.
_comment_liveness_probe: Raw observation backing last_heartbeat, written by the monitor step (steps.monitor.stream_state) on every check. Progress = process alive AND any of the three counters advanced since the previous probe. Needed as stored state because a single observation cannot tell 'advanced' from 'frozen'. jsonl_size is not redundant with jsonl_mtime: Python's buffered writer flushes roughly every 8 KB, so ~200-byte jsonl records can leave mtime minutes behind a healthy process while size still grows. stdout_mtime is the reliable leg — MLClaw owns the redirect to logs/stdout.log and launches with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, so it advances without any cooperation from the training code. observed_at is the ISO timestamp of this probe; it advances every check whether or not the job progressed, so never use it as a liveness signal.
_comment_metrics: Terminal numbers, filled at collect_results. The `best` block is a fixed shape because two things read it without being able to ask: list_runs.py sorts leaderboards on `best.primary_metric_value`, and /train-tune reads it as the stop condition. `primary_metric_value` must be the value of the checkpoint recorded in outputs.best_checkpoint — when the stream's peak epoch was never saved to disk, select_checkpoint.py reports `best_record_skipped` with the value to record here instead. Writing the stream's peak next to a lower-scoring artifact is a fake metric.
_comment_outputs: Canonical artifact paths produced by this run, relative to <run_dir>. Filled by run skills at finalize. Per-stage conventions: training fills best_checkpoint / last_checkpoint / train_log / config_yaml; eval fills report / metrics_json; infer fills predictions / etc. Downstream skills (e.g. /eval-run consuming a train run's best ckpt) read these instead of re-deriving paths from config conventions.
_comment_outcome: Optional. Free-text retrospective written when the run terminates, e.g., 'Refuted. val_loss 0.234 → 0.241 (+3%), convergence epoch 87 → 92'. Pairs with `hypothesis`. Tools must not require this; null is normal.
